# nb1 v0.1.3

Local blink(1) control for people, applications and agents. English is the default, and Chinese guides are under ./zh/. Core source: 48895be5babc11d6f3b2a7ab16e316bd564e726e.

Preview is optional; explicit Play/run validates directly. Action expresses intent; Sequence/Step expresses targets and timing. Keep the original Job ID and endpoint after an uncertain response and query that ID without automatic resubmission. Host Patterns and named colors live on the computer; native device memory is separate.

## Read

- [Install](./install): verified release downloads, optional Homebrew and user services.
- [Get started](./getting-started): install nb1, verify the daemon at http://127.0.0.1:5885/healthz, list devices, open /demo/ and play by serial from CLI or HTTP.
- [API](./api-v1): required fields, defaults, limits, errors and recovery.
- [Raw API Markdown](./source/docs/api-v1.md.txt): original machine-readable text.
- [OpenAPI 3.1](./api-v1.openapi.json): exact released HTTP schema.
- [Agents](./agents): register Codex with `codex mcp add nb1 -- nb1 mcp`, check the connection with `list_devices` and `preview_light`, then use the same daemon for playback. Includes the twelve tools and the optional Skill.
- [Notifications](./agent-notifications): opt-in examples, preview by default.
- [Browser tools](./browser): public WebHID development preview, experimental Chrome extension and ownership handoff. One user-authorized MK2 lit for a one-minute reminder with the popup closed in Chrome for Testing 156 on macOS.
- [Support](./support): system requirements and independently scoped physical evidence.
- [Chinese API](./zh/api-v1): translated explanations with identical identifiers.
- [Source record](./site-info.json): document/build identity.

Local MCP clients launch `nb1 mcp` over stdio. Remote clients can use explicitly enabled HTTPS Streamable HTTP. Both use the official Go MCP SDK and share the daemon's USB connection. The notification helper deliberately uses the CLI. Reading a Skill or this site installs nothing, starts no daemon, enables no hook and requests no hardware permissions. This static site does not control a lamp.

API v1 rejects a competing Job on the same device. A Trigger plays a saved Pattern. Devices execute independently. Public queues, preemption, and device-native deployment remain planned.

The CLI selects the first cached-online configured device in serial order, or the first serial when all are offline. A request with an explicit serial stays bound to that light. HTTP and MCP can omit the serial to apply Trigger and daemon defaults. Look up the original Job ID after an uncertain reply. Read ./trigger-routing for precedence and ./remote-access for configuring HTTPS and tokens.
